name: release-it
summary: A Node.js command that runs a whole release in one go: pick the next version, bump it, commit, tag, push, create a GitHub or GitLab release and publish to npm, asking before each step unless it runs in CI.
intro: Run `npx release-it` and it works out the current version (from `package.json`, else the latest Git tag, else 0.0.0), shows the changelog since the last tag, and asks which version comes next. Then it runs its steps in order: `npm version` to bump `package.json` and the lockfile, `git commit`, an annotated `git tag`, `git push --follow-tags`, a GitHub or GitLab release with the changelog as its notes, and `npm publish`. Interactively it asks for confirmation before each step; with `--ci`, or when it detects a CI environment, it runs them all without prompts, and `--dry-run` prints the commands it would run.

Before starting it checks the repository: by default the working directory must be clean and the branch must have an upstream, and `git.requireBranch` can restrict releases to one branch. Configuration lives in `.release-it.json` or a `release-it` key in `package.json`. Hooks run your own commands at fixed points, named `before:` or `after:` plus a step (`init`, `bump`, `release`) and optionally a plugin (`git`, `npm`, `github`, `gitlab`), so `before:init` can run the tests and `after:bump` can build with the new version number.

Out of the box release-it ignores commit message conventions: its changelog is a `git log` of subjects since the last tag, and you choose the version. Plugins change that. @release-it/conventional-changelog recommends a bump from Conventional Commits and writes CHANGELOG.md, @release-it/bumper reads and writes the version in any file, and others add Keep a Changelog, git-cliff, calendar versioning, .NET or pnpm workspaces. Git, npm, GitHub and GitLab are themselves built-in plugins, and any of them can be switched off with flags like `--no-npm`.
strengths: One command covers the routine of a release, and the interactive mode lets you confirm or skip each step the first few times
Works for any Git project, not only npm packages: turn off the npm plugin and it still bumps, tags, pushes and creates the GitHub or GitLab release
Hooks and plugins at every step make it easy to run tests, builds or extra publishing without wrapper scripts
Supports npm trusted publishing (OIDC) from GitHub and GitLab CI, and staged publishing that defers the 2FA approval to a maintainer
limits: Built around one package per repository: monorepos need the documented monorepo recipe or a workspaces plugin
Version 21 (July 2026) requires Node.js 22 or newer and parses CLI flags strictly, so older Node and loose flags break on upgrade
If a step fails partway, for example the npm publish succeeds but the tag push fails, you finish by hand with `--no-increment` and flags that skip the steps already done
The default changelog is just commit subjects; readable release notes need conventional commits and a plugin, or a hand-written CHANGELOG

story: Releasing a JavaScript package by hand is a fixed sequence that is easy to get wrong: edit the version, commit, tag, push the tag, publish to npm, write the release notes, and do it again next time in the same order. Lars Kappert published release-it to npm in January 2014 as an “interactive release tool for Git repositories”, which could also build and push to a separate distribution repository and publish to npm.

By 1.0.0 in August 2015 the pitch was “bump version, commit, tag, push, publish, done”, with a dry-run mode, a non-interactive mode and GitHub releases; the README noted that release-it had released itself. Later majors kept that core and reshaped everything around it. Versions 9 and 10 dropped the distribution-repository feature. Version 11 (May 2019) introduced plugins, handed the `package.json` bump to `npm version` so lockfiles stay in sync, and rolled back the release commit and tag when a release was cancelled or failed. Version 13 (2020) replaced the old `scripts` with hooks and `--non-interactive` with `--ci`.

Version 15 (April 2022) moved to ES modules and removed anonymous usage metrics. Since then most majors have dropped old Node.js versions; version 21 (July 2026) requires Node.js 22, makes CLI parsing strict and verifies GitLab certificates by default. The latest release is 21.1.1, from October 7, 2026.

choices.choice: Interactive by default, with a CI mode
choices.why: A release is hard to undo, so release-it asks before each commit, tag, push and publish when a person runs it, and only skips the prompts with `--ci` or in a detected CI environment.

The core changelog is plain `git log` output and the version is chosen at the prompt; conventional commits, Keep a Changelog or calendar versioning come in as plugins, so the tool fits projects whatever their commit style.
Delegating to `npm version` updates `package-lock.json` and `npm-shrinkwrap.json` together with `package.json`, instead of release-it editing files itself.

choices.choice: Build the core on its own plugin system (v11)
choices.why: Git, npm, GitHub and GitLab became plugins with lifecycle methods, so third-party plugins can hook into the same steps and any built-in one can be turned off.

timeline.text: First published to npm by Lars Kappert (January 15)
1.0.0 (August 20): bump, commit, tag, push, publish, with dry runs and GitHub releases
11.0.0 (May 1): plugins, `npm version` bumps, rollback on failure
15.0.0 (April 30): ES modules only, anonymous metrics removed
21.0.0 (July 25): Node.js 22 required, strict CLI parsing; 21.1.1 released October 7
